title: Routing-layer drop of stop sequences causing customer-specific overgeneration and eval regressions
creator: Amelia Park
description: Multiple customers reported sudden quality regressions in their prompt evaluations after last week's runtime defaults change and a concurrent routing refactor. Symptoms: long-running responses (overgeneration), missing termination on expected stop tokens, and failing regression tests for customer eval suites. Affected environments: Hosted API (some tenants), Dedicated pools behind proxy routing, and Private deployments using the new request-rewrite plugin. The issue appears only for requests that rely on customer presets (per-tenant generation defaults) that the routing layer merges with incoming requests. Initial hypothesis: the request rewrite/merge code dropped or overwrote the stop sequence(s) when synthesizing the final generation parameters, causing the model to run until token/length limits or different sampling semantics kick in. This ticket tracks triage, mitigation, and the permanent fix.
reproduction_steps:
1) Use customer preset 'legacy-stop-mappings' that sets stop_sequences=["
"] and sampling_mode='greedy'
2) Send a hosted API request that relies on merging request-level generation params with tenant preset via the routing proxy
3) Observe in runtime logs that the final request body to the serving runtime contains sampling_mode but stop_sequences is empty or missing
4) Model output does not terminate on expected stop sequence; customer eval harness shows mismatch with golden outputs
5) Reproduce locally by running the dedicated-proxy with ENABLE_REWRITE=true and the sample request attached in /attachments/repro_request.json
investigation_summary: Root cause: a change in the routing/refactor (commit 7f9a3c) switched to a compact wire format for upstream requests. The merge routine that applies tenant presets to incoming requests used the legacy key 'stop' for single token stop markers; when encountering the newer 'stop_sequences' list field the merge function skipped it. Additionally, the rewrite path flattened nested generation metadata into a header (x-gen-params) and lost the empty-list vs null distinction, causing downstream code to treat missing stop_sequences as 'no termination provided'. Secondary contribution: a separate default sampling-mode change moved some traffic to nucleus sampling which magnified overgeneration when stop signals were missing. Tests added during the refactor didn't include tenant preset merge cases. Evidence: request traces show original client payload included stop_sequences, router request to runtime lacked it, and the model runtime logs show no termination callbacks. A local unit test reproduces the parameter drop consistently.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed to routing-proxy: restore explicit copy of stop_sequences when present and preserve empty-list semantics (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1124)
Temporarily revert hosted default sampling-mode change for flagged tenants via feature flag 'sampling-default-revert'
Engaged Solutions to push tenant-level overrides for the three highest-severity customers (manual override to set stop_sequences in request header)
Added smoke regression to CI that validates tenant preset merge preserves stop_sequences and sampling fields
proposed_fix: Refactor merge code to canonicalize generation parameters and use explicit schema-driven merges (always prefer explicit client-provided fields; merge lists by concatenation/override rules)
Add end-to-end tests (integration) covering hosted, dedicated-proxy and private rewrite plugin flows
Add a lint/check that rejects PRs that change wire encoding of generation parameters without corresponding compatibility adapters
Ship runtime-1.24 patch ensuring model runtime treats absent stop_sequences and empty stop_sequences distinctly
rollout_plan: 1) Merge routing-proxy hotfix to staging and run tenant-presets e2e (24h)
2) Canary to 5% of Hosted traffic + one Dedicated customer pool for 4h, monitor eval mismatch metrics and per-tenant golden set diffs
3) If stable, ramp to 25% then 100% over 12h
4) Backport patch to private deployment package and notify on-prem customers of advisory and available update
5) Run post-rollout sweep to re-run customer eval suites and verify regressions resolved
acceptance_criteria: Customer golden eval suites for affected customers match pre-regression baselines
No increase in overgeneration alerts or token usage anomalies in 48h after full rollout
Integration tests covering tenant-preset merges are green in CI
PRs reviewed and merged, and emergency revert flag removed once metrics stable
